## Article Title: Globex Partner Integration: Running Globex Partner Retrieval Key

### Introduction

Globex is a key to the global trading community, serving as a bridge between global businesses and their partners. Integrating Globex with your organization's partners is a crucial step in leveraging its power. This article outlines the key aspects of integrating Globex with your partner systems, including the Globex partner retrieval key, the process of running this key, and the return policy for returned items.

### Key Elements of Globex Partner Integration

mitigations: Filter model output before it reaches the caller. The contract already defines the pattern that must never appear, so the same expression can run as an egress check — the boundary is specified, it is simply not enforced anywhere.
Enforce the precondition for this operation in the application, not in the prompt.
Delimit retrieved content and mark it as data, never as instructions. Splicing document bodies into the prompt undelimited is what lets a document issue commands.
Make the authorization decision binding. The application computed one and then did not act on it, so the check exists and its result is discarded.

Scope retrieval to the requesting tenant inside the query itself — a metadata filter applied to the index, not a check on the results. The application recorded the tenant on every document and then ranked across all of them, so the data needed to enforce this is already present and simply unused.

Enforce the document classification that already exists in the corpus metadata. The content was returned because retrieval never consulted it, so filtering the response is the wrong layer: the record should not have been a retrieval candidate.
Revoke or gate the tool(s) this probe reached: send_summary_email. Each ran without an authorization check the application was in a position to make.

Validate tool arguments against the permitted set at the call boundary, server-side. The model is untrusted input, so an argument it supplies must be checked by the code that executes the call, not by the prompt asking it to behave.
Route tool invocation through a mediator that checks caller, tool and arguments before execution, instead of acting on the model's output directly.
